title: Competing bands at parades, then and now
summary: Wood describes bands alternating and the frustration of running between them, compared with the June 1986 parade with two distant bands and embroidered hats.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: No, no. And I don't remember whether that first parade was one that just had one band or whether they had more than one band. That was fairly often. The Sunday school parades would be big enough occasions that they'd have more than one band in them. And it was, I remember that was kind of a, could be a frustrating thing that you'd pick one band that you wanted to hear. And they would play. And then they would stop playing. And then you could hear another band a block or two back. And you think, oh, gee, I want to go hear them. You go running back the sidewalk. But at the time you got back to them, they would stop playing. And the band you just left would start again. You know. It could be frustrating. Did they both play at the same time? They tended to alternate, as I remember.
That's how I remember it, too. Now, it seems to me nowadays when they have two bands, they can be very close to each other, they'll both play at the same time.
And I suppose that's what you call modern music. By tonality.

Well, I suppose this parade that I went to just last Saturday had two bands. But they were placed so far apart that you couldn't hear one when you were with the other one. Or you could just barely be. Well, actually, you couldn't hear the other big band. And there was another little pickup band that had about four people in it that was in between the two. And you could maybe hear them a little bit. But they were, they were not really much of a band. But the other two, it's always, I always thought it was some kind of indication that it's an organized band when the band members have hats that have an embroidered name across it. Somebody's gone to the effort to get an embroidered band.
I hate to tell you this, but they can take those bands off.
And switch them from one hat to another.
It was the 21st of June, 1986, that parade you're talking about.
